statement: In equal pyramids which have triangular bases the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights; and those pyramids in which the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights are equal.
heath_proof: For let there be equal pyramids which have the triangular bases ABC, DEF and vertices the points G, H; I say that in the pyramids ABCG, DEFH the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights, that is, as the base ABC is to the base DEF, so is the height of the pyramid DEFH to the height of the pyramid ABCG. For let the parallelepipedal solids BGML, EHQP be completed. Now, since the pyramid ABCG is equal to the pyramid DEFH, and the solid BGML is six times the pyramid ABCG, and the solid EHQP six times the pyramid DEFH, therefore the solid BGML is equal to the solid EHQP. But in equal parallelepipedal solids the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights; [XI. 34] therefore, as the base BM is to the base EQ, so is the height of the solid EHQP to the height of the solid BGML. But, as the base BM is to EQ, so is the triangle ABC to the triangle DEF. [I. 34] Therefore also, as the triangle ABC is to the triangle DEF, so is the height of the solid EHQP to the height of the solid BGML. [V. 11] But the height of the solid EHQP is the same with the height of the pyramid DEFH, and the height of the solid BGML is the same with the height of the pyramid ABCG, therefore, as the base ABC is to the base DEF, so is the height of the pyramid DEFH to the height of the pyramid ABCG. Therefore in the pyramids ABCG, DEFH the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights. Next, in the pyramids ABCG, DEFH let the bases be reciprocally proportional to the heights; that is, as the base ABC is to the base DEF, so let the height of the pyramid DEFH be to the height of the pyramid ABCG; I say that the pyramid ABCG is equal to the pyramid DEFH. For, with the same construction, since, as the base ABC is to the base DEF, so is the height of the pyramid DEFH to the height of the pyramid ABCG, while, as the base ABC is to the base DEF, so is the parallelogram BM to the parallelogram EQ, therefore also, as the parallelogram BM is to the parallelogram EQ, so is the height of the pyramid DEFH to the height of the pyramid ABCG. [V. 11] But the height of the pyramid DEFH is the same with the height of the parallelepiped EHQP, and the height of the pyramid ABCG is the same with the height of the parallelepiped BGML; therefore, as the base BM is to the base EQ, so is the height of the parallelepiped EHQP to the height of the parallelepiped BGML. But those parallelepipedal solids in which the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights are equal; [XI. 34] therefore the parallelepipedal solid BGML is equal to the parallelepipedal solid EHQP. And the pyramid ABCG is a sixth part of BGML, and the pyramid DEFH a sixth part of the parallelepiped EHQP; therefore the pyramid ABCG is equal to the pyramid DEFH. Therefore etc
ai_proof_text:
12.9
**Statement:** In equal pyramids which have triangular bases the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights; and those pyramids in which the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights are equal.

**Step 1.** Let ABCG and DEFH be two pyramids having the triangular bases ABC, DEF and the vertices G, H. First let the pyramids be equal. I say that, as the base ABC is to the base DEF, so is the height of the pyramid DEFH to the height of the pyramid ABCG.

**Step 2.** Through A draw a straight line parallel to BC, and through C a straight line parallel to BA [1.31], and let them meet at M; then ABCM is a parallelogram of which AC is a diameter. In the same way, through D draw a straight line parallel to EF and through F a straight line parallel to ED [1.31], meeting at Q; then DEFQ is a parallelogram of which DF is a diameter. Since the diameter bisects a parallelogram [1.34], the parallelogram ABCM is double the triangle ABC, and the parallelogram DEFQ is double the triangle DEF.

**Step 3.** Through G draw GK parallel to BA and GN parallel to BC [1.31]. Since GK, GN meet one another at G and are parallel to BA, BC, which meet one another at B, and G is not in the plane of ABC (being the vertex of the pyramid), the plane through GK, GN is parallel to the plane through BA, BC, that is, to the plane of the parallelogram ABCM [11.15]. Let the parallelepipedal solid BL be completed, having the parallelogram ABCM as base, BG as an edge, and as the face opposite to the base the parallelogram KGNL lying in the plane through G just described, K, N, L being the vertices over A, C, M respectively (so that AK, CN, ML are parallel to BG). In the same way let the parallelepipedal solid ER be completed, having the parallelogram DEFQ as base, EH as an edge, and as the face opposite to the base the parallelogram OHPR through H, with O, P, R the vertices over D, F, Q.

**Step 4.** The height of the pyramid ABCG is the perpendicular drawn from its vertex G to the plane of its base ABC [D6.4]. The height of the parallelepipedal solid BL is the perpendicular drawn from a vertex of the face KGNL to the plane of the base ABCM; G is such a vertex, and the plane of ABCM is the plane of ABC. Therefore the solid BL has the same height as the pyramid ABCG. In the same way the solid ER has the same height as the pyramid DEFH, namely the perpendicular from H to the plane of DEF.

**Step 5.** The straight lines AC, KN are diagonals of the opposite faces ABCM, KGNL of the solid BL; hence the plane through AC, KN bisects the solid BL [11.28], dividing it into two equal prisms, one of which is the prism having the triangle ABC as base and the triangle KGN as its opposite face. Therefore the solid BL is double this prism. Again, this prism, having a triangular base, is divided into three pyramids equal to one another having triangular bases, one of which is the pyramid having the base ABC and for vertex the point G of the opposite face, that is, the pyramid ABCG [12.7]; therefore the prism is triple the pyramid ABCG. Consequently the solid BL is six times the pyramid ABCG. In the same way the solid ER is six times the pyramid DEFH.

**Step 6.** Now the pyramid ABCG is equal to the pyramid DEFH; hence six magnitudes each equal to the pyramid ABCG are together equal to six magnitudes each equal to the pyramid DEFH [CN2]. But the solid BL is equal to the former and the solid ER to the latter (Step 5); therefore the solid BL is equal to the solid ER [CN1].

**Step 7.** But in equal parallelepipedal solids the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights [11.34]; therefore, as the base ABCM is to the base DEFQ, so is the height of the solid ER to the height of the solid BL.

**Step 8.** Since the parallelogram ABCM is double the triangle ABC and the parallelogram DEFQ is double the triangle DEF (Step 2), the triangle ABC is to the triangle DEF as the parallelogram ABCM is to the parallelogram DEFQ [5.15]. Therefore the triangle ABC is to the triangle DEF as the height of the solid ER is to the height of the solid BL [5.11].

**Step 9.** But the height of the solid ER is the height of the pyramid DEFH, and the height of the solid BL is the height of the pyramid ABCG (Step 4). Therefore, as the base ABC is to the base DEF, so is the height of the pyramid DEFH to the height of the pyramid ABCG; that is, in the equal pyramids ABCG, DEFH the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights.

**Step 10.** Next, let the bases of the pyramids ABCG, DEFH be reciprocally proportional to the heights, so that, as the base ABC is to the base DEF, so is the height of the pyramid DEFH to the height of the pyramid ABCG. I say that the pyramid ABCG is equal to the pyramid DEFH. With the same construction (Steps 2, 3), the parallelograms ABCM, DEFQ are double the triangles ABC, DEF, the solids BL, ER have the same heights as the pyramids ABCG, DEFH (Step 4), and the solids BL, ER are six times the pyramids ABCG, DEFH respectively (Step 5).

**Step 11.** As the parallelogram ABCM is to the parallelogram DEFQ, so is the triangle ABC to the triangle DEF [5.15], and, by hypothesis, so is the height of the pyramid DEFH to the height of the pyramid ABCG, that is, the height of the solid ER to the height of the solid BL. Therefore, as the base ABCM is to the base DEFQ, so is the height of the solid ER to the height of the solid BL [5.11].

**Step 12.** Thus the bases of the parallelepipedal solids BL, ER are reciprocally proportional to their heights; but parallelepipedal solids in which the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights are equal [11.34]. Therefore the solid BL is equal to the solid ER.

**Step 13.** Now the solid BL is six times the pyramid ABCG and the solid ER is six times the pyramid DEFH; the solids being the same multiples of the pyramids, the pyramid ABCG is to the pyramid DEFH as the solid BL is to the solid ER [5.15]. But the solid BL is equal to the solid ER; hence the solid BL is to the solid ER as the solid ER is to the solid ER [5.7]; and the solid ER is to the solid ER as the pyramid DEFH is to the pyramid DEFH [5.15]. Therefore the pyramid ABCG is to the pyramid DEFH as the pyramid DEFH is to the pyramid DEFH [5.11].

**Step 14.** The pyramids ABCG, DEFH thus have the same ratio to the same magnitude, the pyramid DEFH; therefore the pyramid ABCG is equal to the pyramid DEFH [5.9].

**Step 15.** Therefore in equal pyramids which have triangular bases the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights; and those pyramids in which the bases are reciprocally proportional to the heights are equal. Q.E.D.
